shipsOff: research/v2-3/ carries the mechanism behind BACKGROUND_FIDELITY = "off" and is byte-identical to trunk in that state (34/34 parity, and 320/320 fresh artworks unchanged). Nothing is enabled by this batch.

labelMeaning.bf-on: the real published extraction with BACKGROUND_FIDELITY = "on" — a genuine re-run of the full algorithm, not a post-hoc edit of bf-off's colours

bothSidesAreReal: Every palette on both sides is a real extraction of the real artwork, produced by mirror-batch.ts, which refuses to write a label whose name disagrees with the compiled switch. No flag was flipped after the fact and no colour was substituted.

theMechanismUnderTest.summary: Who wins the BACKGROUND role. assignFieldRoles is a strict lexicographic scan over five criteria; frameCoverage (border+corner ownership) is first and populationCoverage is last, so edge ownership pre-empts field mass outright. Two repairs, both gated by the same switch.
theMechanismUnderTest.f1_quantizationBoundary: evidenceLevel is a Math.floor and the comparison was `!== 0`, so two scores differing by an arbitrarily small amount decide the background whenever they straddle a bin boundary. ON requires two levels of separation — the smallest gap that guarantees a real difference wider than one RESOLUTIONS.evidence step. Derived from Math.floor, not tuned.
theMechanismUnderTest.f2_mountReachesTheDecision: The `mount` policy already identifies a frame/matte (owns the border while a materially larger family it encloses owns none) and withdraws its border credit — but only from fieldScore, the FOURTH criterion. The lexicographic scan decides at the FIRST. ON withdraws the same credit from the frame and peripheral criteria, so a positively-identified mount stops winning the background on the one signal it is guaranteed to dominate.
theMechanismUnderTest.f3_mountRatio: mount.minimumEnclosedPopulationRatio moved from 2.5 to 2.09. Needed before F2 can bite on 000ec4aa at all. The incumbent's comment describes a gap of [0.76, 4.47] with the bar at its centre; measuring 479 artworks shows that region is continuously occupied and no such gap exists. The real gap is [1.781, 2.399] — highest review-ACCEPTED frame (000844ca, calib-batch-1a) against lowest review-wants-FLIPPED (000ec4aa) — and 2.09 is its centre. It is also the minimal-blast-radius choice: 4 of 479 artworks are mounts at 2.5, 5 at 2.09, and the fifth is the one review asked for.

whatIsNotUnderTest: Nothing about gradients, foreground, accent, contrast, or midpoints was touched. Where those move in an item they moved because the field pair changed underneath them. Three of the six verdict-backed cases that motivated this arm turned out NOT to be background-selection failures at all (they are surface-representative and treatment-selection failures) and are deliberately absent — see EXPERIMENT.md §'Sub-classes'.

blastRadius.measuredOn: 479 artworks from the UNSCRAMBLED corpus at /Users/Flo/GitHub/palette (159 verdict-carrying + 320 fresh random, drawn deterministically by sha256 of basename from the 7,315 artworks carrying neither a verdict nor a round-8 probe)
blastRadius.note: Figures at the shipped F3 = 2.09. An earlier draft at F3 = 1.58 measured 25/479; the one extra mover exchanged #000000 and #010101.

revertRules.semantics: TRACK_CHARTER.md 'Multiple valid palettes — guardrail semantics' (Flo, 2026-08-02): a mover is a regression only if the destination was itself reviewed negatively or previously compared inferior. Byte-preservation of reviewed-strong outcomes is NOT the bar. Every destination in this batch is unadjudicated, so nothing here auto-fails on arrival; the verdicts decide.
autoKill: ANY item in this batch whose bf-on side is judged worse than its bf-off side AND whose bf-off side is a currently-reviewed-strong palette (disney, 00034b60, 00034b1c) -> that is a mover to a now-known-worse destination. Two or more of those three -> revert F1 entirely and keep only F2+F3.
00034b60's surface collapse judged worse -> F1 must not be applied to criteria other than frameCoverage; re-derive as a frameCoverage-only rule and re-measure.
0013095d judged worse while 000390c0 is judged better -> F1 is the wrong shape. Withdraw it and replace with an explicitly mass-aware arbitration; do not retune the level count.
keep: 000390c0 judged better AND no more than one of the three strong-movers judged worse -> F1 is carrying its weight; propose enabling F1 and re-run the full-corpus census before integration.

000ec4aa judged better -> F2+F3 are independent of F1's fate and can be proposed on their own; they touch only artworks with a positively-identified mount, of which there is 1 in 320 fresh artworks at the incumbent bar.
doNotConclude: Do not read a negative verdict on 000ec4aa as evidence against F1, or vice versa. F1 and F2+F3 fire on disjoint artworks in this batch and can be enabled independently — the policy block and the switch were written so that either can be neutralised without touching the other.
Do not treat the 5.2% blast radius as the cost of F2+F3. Essentially all of it is F1: the mount test fires on 1 artwork in 320 fresh.

honestLimitations: The fix repairs 1 of the 5 off-panel artworks that show the failure pattern (configuration AND massRatio >= 1.5). It is not a fix for the class; it is a fix for two named mechanisms inside the class.

The largest-mass-ratio artwork in the fresh sample (000bd117, massRatio 4.38, a near-white holding 10% of pixels and 75% of the border against a yellow holding 45%) is NOT moved, because its border coverage of 0.749 falls under the mount test's 0.9 bar and its frameCoverage margin is 8 levels. Partial mounts are the named next lead.

F3 is constrained by exactly one measured artwork on each side of its value (000844ca at 1.781, frame accepted; 000ec4aa at 2.399, flip wanted). It is the weakest-evidenced of the three changes; the only reason for confidence in it is that it moves 1 artwork in 479.

The incumbent policy comment for minimumEnclosedPopulationRatio misdescribes its own evidence — it claims a gap that the measured distribution does not contain. Anyone re-tuning that constant from the prose would place it inside an occupied region. The corrected distribution is now recorded in policy.ts.

The 'failure pattern' proxy (background family's field-mass share against the largest chromatic family's) is this arm's construction. It was chosen to match the batch-38 wording and has not itself been validated against review.
